book_meta.work: short stories by Guy de Maupassant and Anton Chekhov
book_meta.author: Maupassant (d. 1893) and Chekhov (d. 1904)
book_meta.status: public domain — retold from the plots, no translation used

sentences.ar: كان اسمه نيكولا توسان، بس ما حدا كان بيعرف اسمه.
sentences.en: His name was Nicolas Toussaint, but no one knew his name.

sentences.ar: كانوا يسموه الجرس، لأنه بيمشي على عكازين، وإجريه بتتأرجح زي الجرس.
sentences.en: They called him the Bell, because he walked on two crutches, his legs swinging like a bell.

sentences.ar: ابن عاهرة ماتت، وبعمر خمستعشر سنة، عربية دعست إجريه.
sentences.en: The son of a whore who died, and at fifteen, a cart ran over his legs.
And since then, he begged.

sentences.ar: من قرية لقرية، على عكازيه، وبياكل اللي بيعطوه، وبينام بالإسطبلات.
sentences.en: Village to village, on his crutches, eating what he was given, sleeping in the stables.

sentences.ar: وما كان بيعرف شي غير هيك.
sentences.en: And he knew nothing else.

sentences.ar: ما بيعرف يقرا، ولا يشتغل، ولا يطلب إلا بإيده.
sentences.en: He could not read, or work, or ask except with his hand.

sentences.ar: وبيوم، الناس بالقرى قرروا إنهم تعبوا منه.
sentences.en: And one day, the people of the villages decided they were tired of him.
They began shutting their doors.
And shouting: every day it is you!
Go and work!
And he grew hungry.
A day, two, three.

sentences.ar: كان يمشي، والدنيا تدور، وبطنه يعصر.
sentences.en: He walked, the world spinning, his belly twisting.

sentences.ar: وبرابع يوم، شاف دجاجة عالطريق، عند مزرعة.
sentences.en: And on the fourth day, he saw a hen on the road, by a farm.
A black hen, pecking in the dust.

sentences.ar: ورمى عليها عكازه، بلا ما يفكر، وضربها، وماتت.
sentences.en: And he threw his crutch at it, without thinking, hit it, and it died.

sentences.ar: وزحف عليها، ومسكها، وحطها تحت قميصه.
sentences.en: And crawled to it, seized it, and put it under his shirt.
And wanted only to light a fire, to eat it.

sentences.ar: وبنفس اللحظة، صاحب المزرعة طلع، وشاف.
sentences.en: And in that same moment, the farmer came out, and saw.
And shouted: thief!

sentences.ar: وركض عليه، وضربه بعصاه على ظهره، وعلى راسه.
sentences.en: And ran at him, and beat him with his stick on the back, on the head.
And the beggar fell, and tried to defend himself with his crutch.
And the farmhands came, and all beat him.
And tied him, and took him to the village, to the lock-up.
And he did not speak.
He did not know how to speak.
He only stared.

sentences.ar: وقال الحارس: بكرا الصبح بيجي الدرك، وبياخدوه للمدينة.
sentences.en: And the guard said: tomorrow morning the gendarmes come, and take him to town.

sentences.ar: ورماه بالحبس، وسكر الباب، وراح يتعشى.
sentences.en: And threw him in the lock-up, locked the door, and went to have supper.

sentences.ar: الحبس أوضة حجر، بلا شباك، بلا فراش، بلا أكل.
sentences.en: The lock-up a stone room, no window, no bed, no food.
And they had taken the hen from him.

sentences.ar: والقرية كلها حكت عنه بالمسا: الشحاد صار حرامي!
sentences.en: And the whole village talked of him that evening: the beggar has become a thief!
Good, rid us of him!
And they slept.
And in the morning, the gendarmes came, and opened the door.

sentences.ar: وكان الجرس مرمي على الحجر، وميت.
sentences.en: And the Bell lay on the stone, dead.
Of hunger.
And everyone was astonished.
No one had thought he was hungry.

sentences.ar: ما حدا فكر إنه لازم ياكل.
sentences.en: No one had thought he must eat.
They had thought of him only as a beggar.
